security_spec.violation_condition: The kernel performs a context switch from a task that has executed ace.enable (setting the ACE-used CSR bit) without first issuing ace.export for each live CC to save its SCC to a per-task buffer, OR the kernel allocates a CC index to a new task without issuing ace.clear on any CC index previously owned by a now-exited task, thereby leaking the prior task's cryptographic context state to the incoming task.
security_spec.summary: ACE CCs are non-renamed per-hart resources whose state persists across context switches unless explicitly exported/cleared; the kernel must save SCC via ace.export on switch-out and restore via ace.import on switch-in, and must ace.clear CCs on task exit to prevent cross-process cryptographic state leakage

findings.finding: The ACE cryptographic extension is not implemented in this kernel. The switch_to macro handles FPU (__switch_to_fpu) and Vector (__switch_to_vector) state save/restore, but has no ACE context-switch logic. No ace_export, ace_clear, or CC-index management exists. Since the ACE ISA extension is absent, the spec violation conditions (leaking SCC to incoming task via missing ace_export/ace_clear across context switches) cannot be triggered.
No ACE CSR definitions (acecsr, sacecsr, or any CC-index management CSRs) exist in the kernel's CSR header. Without CSR definitions, no kernel code can access ACE hardware state.
KVM VCPU run loop has no ACE context save/restore or virtualization. No ACE CSR trapping, no SCC save on VM exit, no SCC restore on VM entry. Since ACE is not implemented, this is expected.

The task's thread_struct has no ACE state fields (no SCC buffer, no CC-index allocation table, no ACE-used bit). Without per-task ACE state storage, there is nothing to save/restore across context switches.
